title: Cheap Client Exorcist
oneLiner: A playful service-business ritual that spots discount vampires, scope-creep ghosts, and lawsuit gremlins before you accept the wrong customer.
targetUser: Freelancers, contractors, agency owners, consultants, stylists, tutors, local-service operators, and SMB buyers assessing whether a customer base is secretly haunted.
keyUx: Paste inquiry messages, budget comments, review behavior, payment terms, and requested exceptions; the app summons client monsters, scores margin danger, suggests boundary scripts, and exports a funny “do not book” talisman.
searchSignals: Reddit r/smallbusiness price increase / cheap customer warning: https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1rcbykx/i_finally_raised_my_prices_by_40_after_3_years_of/
Reddit r/Entrepreneur small-business acquisition hidden problems: https://www.reddit.com/r/Entrepreneur/comments/1mpb95z/has_anyone_here_actually_bought_a_small_business/
stitchPrompt: Design a playful service-business web prototype called Cheap Client Exorcist for freelancers, contractors, agency owners, consultants, stylists, tutors, local-service operators, and small-business buyers who want to avoid margin-killing customers. Users should paste inquiry messages, budget objections, review behavior, payment terms, requested exceptions, and past complaint clues, then summon client monsters, score margin danger, suggest boundary scripts, set a price floor, and export a funny do-not-book talisman. Include a lead message confession box, discount vampire detector, scope-creep ghost trail, payment-lag and complaint omen meter, boundary script spellbook, price-floor courage slider, and shareable exorcism verdict card. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with spooky-cute monster cards, dramatic neon-purple warnings, comic rituals, bold verdict animations, and readable margin math so the prototype feels hilarious, protective, and instantly shareable in small-business communities.
